intro: Picture this: you take the lift up to the rooftop of a 22-storey tower in the middle of Chiang Mai and find an infinity pool whose edge melts into the skyline, the silhouette of Doi Suthep behind it, and below you the buzzing lights of the Night Bazaar — Le Méridien Chiang Mai is the 5-star hotel many people remember as the tall landmark tower on Chang Klan Road · One important thing to know before you book: in 2024 the hotel had a major renovation and was renamed Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel — same building, same location, new look · From around THB 3,400/night, with a real-review score of 4.6/5 from over 5,400 reviews

body.html: Overview and who it's for — Le Méridien Chiang Mai has stood out as a 22-storey tower in the middle of Chiang Mai for years, and it's a name plenty of travellers know well · The first thing to be clear about before booking: in 2024 the hotel went through a major renovation and was rebranded as Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel, while staying the same building, same location, same address on Chang Klan Road · So if you search for "Le Méridien Chiang Mai" and some platforms show it as "Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel," don't be confused — it's the same place · What sets it apart from a typical city hotel is a location within walking distance of the Night Bazaar plus a rooftop pool with Doi Suthep views, a combination that isn't easy to find at this price · Pulling together the real reviews from Tripadvisor, Booking, Agoda, and Trip.com, this place is a great fit for couples, families, solo travellers who want a big full-service hotel, and business travellers who need a downtown hotel with meeting rooms · On the flip side, if you're after the quiet, boutique feel of a garden resort, or a small Lanna-style stay with its own character, this 383-room tower may not be the best answer for you

Location and getting around — Le Méridien / Chiang Mai Marriott sits at 108 Chang Klan Road, Chang Klan, Mueang Chiang Mai, one of the most convenient locations in the city · The advantage every review agrees on is that the hotel is right next to the Chiang Mai Night Bazaar — you walk out the door and you're there, so in the evening you can shop for souvenirs, grab street food, catch a show, and head back to your room without ever hailing a ride · Chang Klan Road is also packed with restaurants, massage shops, convenience stores, and several more night markets within walking distance · To reach the walled Old City, Tha Phae Gate, and the famous temples is about a 5–10 min drive · One Nimman and the Nimman area are around 10–15 min away · A point many people love is that it's only about 4 km from Chiang Mai Airport (CNX), a 10–15 min drive, ideal for a short trip where you land and want to get to your room fast · Around the hotel there are several more markets and points of interest within walking distance, including Anusarn Market with its seafood and souvenirs, affordable Thai massage shops, and cafés that open early, so it's easy to find something to eat in the morning without much planning · If you like morning markets, Warorot Market (Kad Luang) isn't far either, just a few minutes by red songthaew or Grab · One thing to be aware of about the location: the Chang Klan area is lively and very busy at night, so a lower-floor or street-facing room may pick up some of the bustle, and evening traffic is fairly heavy, so leave extra time if you have appointments — more on the noise in the notes below

Room types and decor — The hotel has 383 rooms and suites across a 22-storey tower, in several tiers · The Deluxe Room is the entry-level option at around 36 sqm, which is more spacious than the entry rooms at many 5-star hotels in Chiang Mai · Above that is the King Room / Premium Room, which adds city and Doi Suthep views on the higher floors · The Executive / Club Room tier comes with M Club Lounge access plus snacks and drinks throughout the day · And the Suite is the largest, with a separate sitting area for special celebrations or business trips · After the 2024 renovation the rooms were redone in a bright, easy-on-the-eyes palette, a contemporary modern style with hints of Lanna, a change from the darker tones of before · What guests praise often is the floor-to-ceiling windows that open onto city and mountain views, the blackout curtains that keep the room dark and quiet for sleeping, and the spacious, clean bathrooms · Rooms have a coffee machine, minibar, Smart TV, and free drinking water · An honest note from the reviews: because it's a large building, some reviews mention small things like upkeep in certain rooms or a few fixtures starting to show wear, so if the view matters to you, ask for a high-floor room on the Doi Suthep side when you book · Another thing many guests appreciate is the soft, comfortable beds and bedding you'd expect from a big chain, plus bathrooms with a clearly separate shower area — some higher-tier rooms have a soaking tub · The rooms are well laid out, with a work desk for anyone who needs to sit and work or take online meetings, and plenty of power outlets · For families with children, the hotel has extra beds and services you can ask about, but most rooms are designed mainly for two, so if you're travelling as a larger group, check the room type and number of beds carefully when booking
"The room was so quiet at night thanks to the blackout curtains — I slept great. And the moment you step out of the hotel you're at the Night Bazaar. So convenient."

Facilities, pool, and spa — The highlight every review agrees on is the rooftop infinity pool, its edge melting into the skyline, with views over the whole of Chiang Mai and the silhouette of Doi Suthep behind · The standout is that the pool is big enough to actually swim and relax in, not just a photo pool, and many people rate it one of the best-atmosphere rooftop pools in Chiang Mai, especially at sunset · Beside the pool is the Pool House, a poolside bar serving botanical cocktails and mocktails, perfect for an evening drink · Beyond the rooftop there's a fully equipped fitness room, a relaxing spa and massage service, and for business travellers or seminar groups, the hotel has 11 meeting rooms and the M Club Lounge for higher-tier guests · Free parking and free Wi-Fi throughout · Overall the facilities are complete for a big city hotel — there's no water park or full kids' club, but there's enough pool and common space for families to relax comfortably

Food and bars — The hotel's main restaurant is Latest Recipe, an international all-day dining venue serving everything from the breakfast buffet to à la carte lunch and dinner, open daily around 9:00 AM–11:00 PM · Breakfast here is something guests bring up a lot — a varied buffet with Thai, Asian, and Western dishes, egg and live-cooking stations, and a fruit and bakery corner, with many saying the selection is wide and the quality is good for a 5-star price · There's also the Pool House bar on the rooftop and seating for drinks inside the hotel · An honest note from the reviews: during high season when the hotel is full, the breakfast room can get crowded and you may have to wait for a table at peak hours, so it's best to head down before the rush — or, if you'd rather take it easy, the hotel's spot next to the Night Bazaar means there are plenty of restaurants and street food to choose from within walking distance

Service — The thing that gets the most praise and is clearly this place's strength is the staff service · A great many reviews describe the staff the same way: warm, smiling, attentive, and often going beyond expectations, from the welcome at the front desk to help with getting around to the poolside and restaurant teams · Plenty of international travellers say this is the reason they come back to stay again · The concierge is good at hailing cars, booking tours, and recommending places to visit · For Marriott Bonvoy members, since the rebrand to the Marriott brand you now get member benefits according to your tier, an added plus for anyone already collecting points with the chain · Overall, if there's one thing keeping this place's satisfaction scores consistently high, service is the answer

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — On the praise side, the things mentioned again and again are the location next to the Night Bazaar that makes getting around so easy, the rooftop pool with genuinely lovely Doi Suthep views, rooms that are clean, spacious, and quiet thanks to the blackout curtains, the wide breakfast selection, and staff service that's warmer than expected · On the notes side, found in some reviews, are prices that climb fairly fast and run high in high season compared with local alternatives, the breakfast room getting crowded at peak hours, pool water that's on the cold side on some days with leaves blowing in from nearby trees, and a few reviews feeling that when it's very busy, some service points can slow down relative to what you're paying · Across over 5,400 reviews the average still scores a high 4.6 out of 5 and ranks it among the top hotels in Chiang Mai, which shows the positives outweigh the notes for most travellers

Price comparison and value — The starting price for a Deluxe Room is around THB 3,400–THB 4,500/night in normal periods, and can climb to THB 6,000–THB 8,000+ in high season (November–February) or during major festivals, while Suite and Club rooms run higher depending on the benefits included · Compared with other downtown 5-star hotels, the value here lies in getting a location next to the Night Bazaar + a rooftop pool + international-level service at a price that's usually lower than luxury boutiques or Ping River resorts · If you plan to spend most of your time exploring the city on foot and want a big hotel where everything's right there when you step out, the money is well spent · But if you mean to spend most of your time at the property relaxing resort-style, you may want to weigh up the riverside or out-of-town options that offer a different atmosphere · The tip is to compare prices across several platforms and book with free cancellation first, since rates move quite a bit by date and festival period

What to know before booking, and the bottom line — In short, Le Méridien Chiang Mai (now Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel) is a 5-star downtown hotel that suits people who want a convenient walkable location plus the comfort of a big hotel, good service, and that signature rooftop pool · Things to know before booking: one — the brand name has changed to Marriott, so search both names to compare prices · two — ask for a high-floor room on the Doi Suthep side if you want the view and quiet · three — in high season, book ahead and lock in your rate · four — to avoid a crowded breakfast room, head down before the peak · five — if you're travelling as a group or large family, ask about interconnecting rooms when booking, as there are a limited number and they go fast · six — if you're driving yourself or renting a car, the plus is free parking, but evening traffic in the Chang Klan area is fairly heavy, so leave extra travel time · For couples, families, and business travellers who want a full-service downtown hotel at an affordable price, this is one of the safest and best-value choices in Chiang Mai · And if you're already a Marriott Bonvoy member, staying within this chain is an extra edge that makes the trip even more worthwhile

honestSummary: Le Méridien Chiang Mai (now Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel) is the best downtown 5-star choice for anyone who wants a convenient walkable location next to the Night Bazaar plus a rooftop pool and international-level service at an affordable price · But you have to accept that it's a high-rise hotel in a lively area, not a quiet garden resort, and high-season prices climb fast
honestChecks: If you're after the quiet atmosphere of a garden resort or a small Lanna-style stay with character — this is a lively 383-room high-rise in the city centre → consider a Ping River resort or a boutique stay in the Old City instead

If you're sensitive to noise and want total quiet — the Chang Klan area is busy at night, and low-floor street-side rooms may pick up noise → ask for a high-floor room on the Doi Suthep side when you book

If you're booking in high season (Nov–Feb) or during a major festival — prices climb fast and the good rooms fill up early → book ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate first, then compare across several platforms

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Le Méridien Chiang Mai (Chiang Mai Marriott)

faq.q: Is Le Méridien Chiang Mai still open · why do some places list it as Chiang Mai Marriott?
faq.a: It's still open, in the same building and same location · In 2024 the hotel had a major renovation and was rebranded as Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel · If you search "Le Méridien Chiang Mai" and some platforms show it as "Chiang Mai Marriott Hotel," it's the same place — we recommend searching both names to compare prices

faq.q: Where is Le Méridien Chiang Mai · how close is it to the Night Bazaar?
faq.a: It's located at 108 Chang Klan Road, Chang Klan, Mueang Chiang Mai · It's right next to the Chiang Mai Night Bazaar — you walk out the door and you're there · It's about a 7–10 min drive from the Old City and Tha Phae Gate, and only 10–15 min from Chiang Mai Airport

faq.q: What's the starting price at Le Méridien Chiang Mai · what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 3,400/night for a Deluxe Room of ~36 sqm · There are several tiers, from Deluxe, Premium/King, and Executive/Club (with M Club Lounge access) up to the Suite · Prices depend on the period and package — they climb fast in high season, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: What's the pool like at Le Méridien Chiang Mai?
faq.a: It's a rooftop infinity pool whose edge melts into the skyline, overlooking the Chiang Mai city view and the silhouette of Doi Suthep · The pool is big enough to relax and swim in, with the Pool House poolside bar · The atmosphere is best at sunset · Note: the water is on the cold side some days and leaves may blow in

faq.q: Who is Le Méridien Chiang Mai best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, families, solo travellers, and business travellers who want a big full-service hotel downtown with easy access to the Night Bazaar · If you're after the quiet atmosphere of a garden resort or a small Lanna-style boutique stay, a place by the Ping River or in the Old City may suit you better

faq.q: What's breakfast like at Le Méridien Chiang Mai?
faq.a: Breakfast is served at the international Latest Recipe restaurant — a buffet with a varied selection of Thai, Asian, and Western dishes, live-cooking stations, fruit, and bakery · Many reviews praise the quality as good for a 5-star price · Note: in high season when the hotel is full it can get crowded at peak hours, so we recommend going down early
